title: reading-notes-llm-conference-iclr-2025-hannah-lee
content:
ICLR 2025 - quick reading notes and takeaways (personal)

Context / goal:
- Capture ideas relevant to Redwood inference runtime: low-latency kernels, batching strategies, quantization tradeoffs, and evals that are practical for production.
- Short list of experiments to prioritize before next infra sprint.

Highlights / interesting papers
- FlashAttention 2 / efficient attention kernels
  - Faster attention kernels still matter for medium sequences (256-1024). Gains are obvious on recent A100/NVIDIA hw but need careful integration for mixed-precision + quantized pipelines.
  - Implementation note: need to compare memory usage and peak allocator behavior; potential to reduce KV copy overhead by 1-2x.
- Speculative Decoding (sampling with a cheap model to propose tokens)
  - Big win for tail latency when serving highest-percentile requests. But needs robust fallback. If we integrate, must measure quality regression on our reranker/QA workloads.
- Adaptive quantization and per-channel QAT-like schemes
  - Papers showing per-layer/static calibration + small fine-tune give much better FP-equivalent quality at 4-bit. For Redwood Optimize, this could be a recommendation path (profiles per model + workload).
- Dynamic batching / latency-aware batching schedulers
  - New scheduler ideas that incorporate latency SLOs and variance estimates. Prefer schedulers that can operate with small state and be replicated across nodes.

Practical takeaways for Redwood
- Kernel integration:
  - Try FlashAttention 2 reference on our internal kernel-bench (TODO below). Measure: throughput @ 256/512/1024 seq, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU memory pressure.
  - Watch out for kernel stalling when KV cache + streaming responses are used together.
- Speculative decode experiments:
  - Build a minimal pipeline: small student model (quantized) proposes candidates -> large model verifies. Evaluate end-to-end latency and tok/sec.
  - Key metric: fraction of tokens accepted vs verified + quality delta on our chat benchmark.
- Quantization profiles + rollout plan:
  - Create per-model profile recipes (embedding, attn, mlp) that we can attach in model catalog metadata.
  - For Dedicated customers, offer a graded rollout: opt-in alpha (no SLA), then beta with SLA discount if adoption.
- Observability and evaluation:
  - Need token-level differences for quality monitoring after deploying quantized kernels. Hook this into Redwood Console's rollouts feature.

Notes / fragments from talks
- "Cost-aware routing" talk: emphasize shipping transparent numbers to customers (cost per 1k tokens under each profile). This is consistent with our product thesis.
- "SLO-driven batching": interesting approach - batching decisions driven by live SLO violation probability estimates; might be heavy but could be approximated with EWMA of queue times.
- Panel on benchmarking: community needs standardized tail-latency testbeds (not just throughput). Proposal: create a lightweight benchmark harness that runs per-model scenarios (chat vs completion vs embeddings) with configurable concurrency distributions.

Open questions / risks
- How brittle are speculative-decoding accept thresholds across domains? If we tune on chat convos we might break code-gen or math prompts.
- Quantization-induced calibration drift over time (model updates). Need auto-recalibration hooks when model version changes.
- Kernel compatibility matrix explosion: combining quantized kernels + flash kernels + per-device specializations leads to many supported variants. Need better metadata and auto-selection fallback hierarchy.

TODO / next steps (short-term)
- [ ] Create kernel-bench PR with FlashAttention2 baseline on our harness (owner: Hannah). Linked: github PR in linked_artifacts.
- [ ] Prototype speculative decode pipeline on a small Llama-like model; synthetic traffic with long-tail tokens (owner: Marco).
- [ ] Draft Confluence page summarizing benchmarking plan and metrics for infra sprint (owner: Evelyn).
- [ ] Add metric hooks for token-level regression alerts to Console (tracked in JIRA-ENG-6789).

Random notes to self
- Remember to ping infra about GPU allocator knobs (CUDA mem pool) - allocator fragmentation skewed results in past microbenchmarks.
- Check upstream kernel license before shipping in Dedicated (OSS header + attribution).

Links to papers / slides referenced (quick copy)
- FlashAttention: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.00851
- Speculative Decoding overview (slides): https://example.com/spec-decoding-slides
- SLO-driven batching (paper): https://example.com/slo-batch-paper

End of notes. Keep this doc messy - it's a scratchpad. Will clean some sections into Confluence once experiments produce data.
